title: Record K198.8m frozen under proceeds of crime law
detail: Police, the Public Prosecutor and BPNG's FASU, via the ARROW working group, froze K198.8 million across multiple bank accounts in a multi-year fraud probe; Commissioner David Manning called it the largest amount ever frozen by police.
attribution: Police Commissioner David Manning via RPNGC

title: Police target 'Don't Care Gang' in Popondetta
detail: Commissioner David Manning said the self-styled 'Don't Care Gang' attacking communities around Bakubari village was a priority target and police would use Criminal Code and Counter-Terrorism Act powers against it.

title: FATF places PNG on grey list
detail: FATF placed Papua New Guinea under increased monitoring after its Mexico City plenary; BPNG said NEC directed 23 agencies to implement the action plan, with a first progress update due September 2026.
agency: Bank of Papua New Guinea / FATF
attribution: BPNG Governor Elizabeth Genia and NCC co-chairs via BPNG

title: NWS puts Jiwaka on drought alert, highlands on watch
detail: PNG National Weather Service placed Jiwaka on drought alert and Chimbu, Enga, Hela, NCD and Western Highlands on drought watch, expecting below-average rain in the highlands and Western Province.

title: TIPNG: prosecutions key to exiting grey list
detail: Transparency International PNG said the state's failure to prosecute money-laundering offenders is the main barrier to leaving the FATF grey list and urged quarterly progress reports on the 23 agencies.

title: Five killed in Goilala village violence; police gun stolen
detail: Five people including an auxiliary police officer were killed at Lio village over a compensation dispute, and a police firearm went missing; Central PPC Chief Inspector Joseph Salle said weather and roads hampered deployment.

title: 54 arrested in Upper Highlands firearms and terrorism sweep
detail: Police said coordinated operations made 54 arrests in Enga, Nipa, Jiwaka, Wapenamanda and elsewhere, including over destruction of Mabisanda Lutheran Rural Hospital, seizing M4/M16 rifles and charging under the Counter-Terrorism Act 2024 and Firearms Act.
attribution: Police Commissioner David Manning via RPNGC

title: GI-TOC: PNG laundering threat up to US$1.4bn a year
detail: Global Initiative estimated money-laundering threats at US$560 million to US$1.4 billion a year, citing logging, fisheries, gold smuggling (~US$34m/yr) and a reported US$3 million airport gold theft in February 2026, with fewer than five successful ML prosecutions in two decades.
srcname: Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime

title: Severe TC Maila hits Bougainville and eastern PNG
detail: Tropical Cyclone Maila peaked at Category 5 on 8 April with sustained winds reported at 215 km/h while stalling over the Solomon Sea; at least 11 deaths were confirmed by 13 April and more than 10,000 people affected, with nearly 20,000 needing assistance in Bougainville; eight died in a single landslide at Asiko village, Central Bougainville.
agency: Tropical Cyclone Warning Centre Port Moresby
attribution: TCWC Port Moresby / Australian BoM data and PNG government statements via The Watchers

title: Lamarain landslide kills 10 in East New Britain
detail: A large deep-seated landslide triggered by TC Maila rainfall struck Lamarain in Inland Baining LLG, killing 10 people and injuring 18, with multiple other fresh failures nearby.
attribution: Landslide analysis by The Landslide Blog

title: Soldiers blockade roads near Murray Barracks
detail: A group of PNGDF soldiers set up roadblocks near Murray Barracks in protest over alleged recruitment nepotism and disciplinary charges against whistleblowers; PM Marape announced a two-week recruitment probe with an Australian officer taking part.
attribution: PM Marape and PNGDF statements via ABC

title: PNGDF imposes nationwide close camp
detail: Chief of Defence Rear Admiral Philip Polewara issued Directive No. 7 of 2026 imposing a one-month close camp on all PNGDF units, restricting barracks movement, military vehicle use and weapons distribution after the soldiers' protest.

title: Sambio village massacre kills 12 in Bulolo
detail: Twelve people were killed and six houses burned at Sambio village; after a two-month task force probe 27 men were arrested, 25 charged with 12 counts of wilful murder and two with arson, and four factory-made firearms seized.
attribution: Morobe PPC Chief Supt Samson Siguyaru via RPNGC

title: Court orders Kandep tribal ceasefire
detail: The National Court at Wabag ordered a binding ceasefire between two clans in Kandep, requiring weapons to be laid down and a peace agreement within 14 days; police and PNGDF were deployed to enforce it.
attribution: National Court order and Enga PPC via RPNGC

title: Laiagam compensation ceremony turns deadly
detail: A clan withdrew from a compensation exchange and opened fire, killing two; a retaliatory attack next morning killed a schoolboy. Enga PPC Chief Supt Steven Harris urged an end to payback killings.

title: Police debunk fake NCD water-outage emergency
detail: NCD/Central Commander Benjamin Turi said a viral message claiming an NCD state of emergency and 14-day water outage was false; police sent a team to the Sogeri water source to assess conditions amid the dry spell.

title: 20 Correctional Services officers arrested in Port Moresby
detail: Twenty CS personnel were arrested and charged with illegal firearm discharge, assault and threats after a confrontation spread from a CS barracks to a residence; Police Minister Sir John Pundari called it unacceptable.
attribution: Police Minister and Commissioner via RPNGC

title: Bougainville submits final independence position
detail: ABG President Ishmael Toroama handed Bougainville's Final Position Paper to the independent facilitator and PNG's Chief Secretary, proposing preparation until 1 Sept 2027, then self-government, and full independence by 2030.

title: Two boats capsize off Kokopo; 27 lost
detail: Two boats returning from Pangpang Island (Duke of York Islands) to Kokopo capsized in rough seas in St George's Channel; 27 people (14 children) were lost, 13 bodies recovered, and the search was called off on 14 August. Authorities then capped boats at 8-10 passengers with convoy departures.
place: St George's Channel, near Pigeon Island

title: Nembi Plateau tribal fight halted by police
detail: Fighting broke out between two council wards at Embi village, Nembi Plateau LLG; Southern Highlands PPC Chief Inspector Kelly Sombe said both sides agreed to lay down weapons and prepare peace talks. No deaths reported.

title: Four killed in Yangoru payback murders
detail: Four people from Haripmo village were killed in a string of murders including a retaliatory double killing; police arrested four suspects, East Sepik PPC Supt Christopher Tamari said.

title: Ex-UPNG bursar charged over system fraud
detail: NFACD said a former University of PNG bursar was arrested on a warrant over unauthorised access to university systems and fraudulent transfers totalling about K602,786, plus about K445,860 in losses from fraudulent student registrations.
attribution: NFACD Director Robert Volo via RPNGC

title: Western Highlands governor warns of severe dry season
detail: Governor Wai Rapa said the El Nino-linked dry season was 'on another scale', with the river supplying Mount Hagen's water drying up, and said the province lacked resources to cope.
attribution: Governor Wai Rapa via Asia Pacific Report

title: Cabinet releases drought funds; NCD and Gulf critical
detail: Minister Billy Joseph announced K10 million per province (PSIP) and K5 million per district (DSIP) for El Nino drought response; NCD and Gulf were rated extreme/critical and a dozen other provinces on severe alert.
attribution: Minister for Health and National Disaster Services via PNG Today

title: Three arrested over fake gold sales in Tari
detail: Hela police said suspects sold a fake 109 g gold piece for K202,000 and were intercepted trying to sell a 1,245.5 g fake piece valued at K2.31 million; the PPC warned millions of kina in counterfeit gold may be circulating in Porgera and other mining areas.
attribution: Hela PPC Inspector Arau Mairi via RPNGC

title: Six OBT gang members charged near Nadzab
detail: A dawn operation at Ngarumutu near Nadzab detained 11 suspected members of the OBT group; six were charged with possessing homemade firearms, ammunition, offensive weapons and marijuana.

title: Kidnapping and murder of teen girl in Western Province
detail: Armed criminals kidnapped two teenage girls near Haiyafuli village, Mogulu; one was killed and the other held at gunpoint, and one offender was killed in the police response, Commissioner David Manning said.
